mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of such episodes, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in triggered periods, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% in the same month signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes real earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such co-triggered months, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -1% in the same month
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in triggered months, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which initially boosts consumer spending but eventually increases wage and input costs, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in an otherwise neutral macro environment.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for three consecutive months
regime_hint: neutral macro environment (no major policy or demand shock)
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) in triggered periods under neutral regimes, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above 0.8% for four consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of the monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in at least 60% of triggered periods, the hypothesis is falsified.
